{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. {{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

revision.text:
{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

revision.text:
{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

revision.text:
{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == Related Topics == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

{{Infobox ancient site |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |Caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |Latitude = 35.5733 |Longitude = 135.1014 |Shape = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |Era = Early 5th century |Structure = |Size = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |Burial = Female |Artifacts = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |Special Notes = Features distinctive artifacts associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

The excavated sarcophagus and artifacts are designated as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated artifacts, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. Artifacts including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period burial mounds with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == Structure == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == Artifacts == Artifacts include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Buried Individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period burial mound groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture) == See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kofun in Kyoto Prefecture]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Scallop-shaped tumuli]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Zenpokoenfun]] [[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:dd]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:kk]][[Category:Kyōtango]] Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}
