'''大谷古墳'''（おおたにこふん）は、[[京都府]][[京丹後市]][[大宮町 (京都府)|大宮町]]谷内小字大谷にある[[古墳]]。[[帆立貝形古墳|帆立貝式]]の[[前方後円墳]]である{{Sfn|京丹後市編さん委員会|2010}}。出土石棺及び出土遺物は京丹後市[[指定文化財]][https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物]（京丹後市教育委員会「京丹後市デジタルミュージアム」）。 == 概要 == [[竹野川]]を見下ろす丘陵先端に単独で築造された古墳である。出土品類から５世紀前半の築造と推定されている。被葬者の完全な人骨が遺存し、人骨が[[熟年]][[女性]]であることが特徴として挙げられる{{Sfn|京丹後市編さん委員会|2010|p=143}}。このことから、当地域は古墳時代中期のある時期、女性首長による統治が行われていたとする説もある{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=31}}。また、支配者を象徴する鏡・玉・剣の[[三種の神器]]が出土している{{Sfn|古代丹後の里資料館|2013|p=18}}。女性首長を葬った古墳は[[熊本県]][[宇土市]]の[[向野田古墳]]、[[大分県]][[大分市]]の[[築山古墳 (大分市)|築山古墳]]など数例しかない{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=31}}。そのため、発掘当時は「[[丹後国|丹後]]の[[卑弥呼]]」と比喩され話題になった{{Sfn|古代丹後の里資料館|2013|p=18}}。また、移築に備えた作業中に、墳丘盛土の下層から[[弥生時代]]の台状墓に伴う主体部が4基重複（合計6基）した状態で確認されている{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=7}}。 == 発掘の経緯 == [[1987年]]（[[昭和]]62年）、[[京都府]][[中郡 (京都府)|中郡]][[大宮町 (京都府)|大宮町]]の企業造成予定地として、大宮町字谷内小字大谷地区が選ばれた{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987}}。予定地内には周知の[[遺跡]]は存在しないとされていたが、丘陵地での大規模工事であるため、京都府教育委員会文化財保護課の協力を得て、予定地及び周辺の詳細な遺跡分布調査を実施した。この時、存在が確認された遺跡の一つが大谷古墳である{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987}}。大谷古墳ほか4箇所の遺跡の発見により、大宮町教育委員会は大宮町産業課に対し、[[工業団地]]造成予定計画の変更を求め、協議を行った{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987}}。その結果、4箇所の遺跡については極力現状のままで保存することになったが、造成予定地の中心部に位置する大谷古墳については、設計上現状保存が困難とされ、記録保存を前提とする発掘調査を実施することになった{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987}}。 == 規模 == [[File:Ootani-kofun2.jpg|thumb|200px|大谷古墳石棺]] 規模に比べて前方部が短い[[帆立貝式古墳|帆立貝式]]の[[前方後円墳]]であり、[[埴輪]]・[[葺石]]・段築はない{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987}}。 ; 墳丘 * 全長32メートル * 後円部径26メートル * 前方部幅19メートル * 基底部からの高さ ** 後円部4メートル ** 前方部2.5メートル * 墳丘の裾部 ** 幅約1.5メートル ; 墳頂部 * 直径12.5メートル × 短径11メートルの主軸方向に長い不整な円形 == 出土品 == [[ファイル:大谷古墳 (京丹後市) 出土品.JPG|thumb|300px|right|{{center|出土品}}{{small|丹後古代の里資料館展示。}}]] 古墳に伴う遺物 * [[銅鏡]]1面:面系10.8センチメートル、縁面0.4センチメートル、反り0.2センチメートル。極めて保存状態が良い{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=25}}。 * [[勾玉]]1点:緑色半透明を呈する良質な硬玉製品「C」字型。腹部に未調整面がある{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=25}}。 * ガラス小玉33点:青色を呈する臼玉状品{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=26}}。 * 鉄剣1本:両関。断面はレンズ状を呈している。身の一部に布目痕、茎の一部に木質が遺存する。全長43.7センチメートル、刃部長33.9センチメートル、最大幅3.0センチメートル、厚さ0.5センチメートル、茎部長9.6センチメートル{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=25}}。 * 鉄斧1点:[[鍛造]]の袋状鉄斧。袋状の成型は粗雑である。全長7.2センチメートル、刃幅3.3センチメートル{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=26}}。 * [[刀子]]1点:{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987}} ** 男性被葬者には複数の刀剣が副葬されるのに対して、女性副葬者では1本に限定されるなど、刀剣類の副葬数に性差が存在する{{Sfn|清家|2010}}。 [[弥生時代]]の遺物（下層部の弥生時代墳墓） * [[弥生土器]]:[[壺]]、[[甕]]、高坏等の器形がある{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=26}}。 * [[鉄鏃]]1点:木葉形の鏃身に茎がつくものと考えられている{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=28}}。 [[石棺]] * [[花崗岩]]質の地山を切り出した部分、墳丘の主軸と直交する方向に、組合式石棺が営まれている{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=15}}。 * 墓壙は長さ4.55メートル、幅2.8メートル、北東辺の一部に張り出した部分は階段と見られている{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=15}}。 * 深さは約1メートル、石棺材を添えつける位置のみ溝状に彫り凹められている{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=15}}。 * 内部は[[弁柄]]で一面[[えんじ色]]に塗られていた京都新聞2007年6月5日。[[粘土]]等で石材隙間が密閉され千数百年にわたり土砂の流入を防いできた為、保存状態が良かったと推測される佐藤仁成、中江忠宏著『もっと知りたい伝えたい丹後の魅力』2008年、p. 18。 == 人骨 == 足首を除くほぼ全身各部の骨が残存した状態で発見されたが破損は著しかった{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=33}}。寛骨の形状から女性と判定され、[[大臼歯]][[歯冠]]の摩耗が著しく、腰椎椎体の前面に経度の嘴状骨増殖が認められることから死亡年齢が熟年前半と推定される{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=34}}。他地域で同時期に発見された女性の人骨と比較し、著しく長い脳頭蓋、極端に低い顔面、鼻といった特徴から[[縄文人]]的色彩が強い{{Sfn|大宮町教育委員会|1987|p=35}}。 == 女性祭祀者 == [[記紀]]にも記述されている様に、第9代[[開化天皇]]の[[妃]]である竹野媛、第11代[[垂仁天皇]]の[[后]]である[[日葉酢媛]]を輩出し、大谷古墳近くの[[丹後国]][[二之宮]]でる[[大宮売神社]]に祀られる[[天鈿女神]]（[[大宮売神]]）や[[比沼麻奈為神社]]に祀られる[[豊受大神]]も女性神であることから、古代丹後は女性の地位が高かったことが推測される{{Sfn|古代丹後の里資料館|2013|p=33}}（当地の[[式内社]]の[[祭神]]は全て豊受大神。大宮売神社の祭神二座の内の一座である若宮売神は豊受大神と同一神とされ[http://www.shiga-miidera.or.jp/serialization/shinra/124.htm 三井寺-公式サイト]、波彌神社の祭神は[[武埴安彦命]]であるが元来は豊受大神とされる[http://engishiki.org/tango/bun/tag390303-01.html 延喜式神社の調査]）。近年、神社そのものが前方後円墳であることが判明している『角川日本地名大辞典 上巻』656頁 昭和56年大宮売神社は古代祭祀場から神社へと発展したものであり [https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/1/4911.html 京丹後市デジタルミュージアム] - 公式サイト、[[1879年]]（[[明治]]12年）に二の[[鳥居]]の下から壷や[[曲玉]]・[[勾玉]]が発見されている。これらの品は祭事の跡（[[3世紀]]頃:弥生時代後期）を物語っている。大宮売神は[[巫女]]（[[シャーマン]]）であり、曲玉や勾玉は木の枝につけて[[祈祀]]の道具とした。これらのことからも女性祭祀者でなかったかと考えられる。大谷古墳も弥生時代墳墓を下層遺構とする古墳であり大宮売神社と同様に弥生時代の遺物が発掘されている。 == 丹後の弥生墳丘墓の独自性 == [[丹後王国論]]を提唱する歴史学者の[[門脇禎二]]（[[京都府立大学]]名誉教授）は、[[竹野川]]流域を中心とした政治領域があったと考察している{{PDFlink|[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/material/files/group/43/lib1l.pdf 古代丹後の原風景]}}。その論の特徴の一部に先述したトヨウケモチ（豊受大神）信仰、竹野川流域の丘陵地で見られる方形台状墓は丹後を起源とする論じている。[[丘陵地]]の突端の斜面を削り出した台状墓は弥生時代後期の丹後・但馬の独自のものであり出雲を中心とした[[因幡]]、[[伯耆]]、[[越]]で見られる[[山陰]]を代表する[[四隅突出型墳丘墓]]は[[丹後国|丹後]]・[[但馬国|但馬]]では見られない。この事から[[出雲]]とは一線を画する独自[[文化圏]]を持った勢力があったと考えられている{{PDFlink|[http://www3.city.toyooka.lg.jp/kokubunjikan/news/news23.pdf 但馬国府・分国寺館ニュース第3号　2011.3]}}。これらの台状墓は大谷古墳がある近隣の竹野川上流部域の丘陵地帯に大谷古墳も含め三坂神社墳墓群、左坂古墳群、今市古墳群、比丘尼屋敷墳墓などの台状墓が狭い地域内で多数発見されている[http://wi12000.starfree.jp/forGmap/html/kyo_tango_yayoi.html 京丹後の弥生遺跡] 。 == 周辺地域の類似事例 == [[7世紀]]の[[令制国]]成立以前は[[丹後国]]と同国であった[[但馬国]]内の[[兵庫県]][[朝来市]][[和田山町]]にある向山古墳群の2号墳より、古墳時代前期の女性首長と思われる人骨が発掘されている。大臼歯歯冠の摩耗が著しく推定年齢は40～60歳、奥歯がなく[[虫歯]]の痕があり、推定身長は木棺の大きさより150cmとされる[https://koukohaku.blogspot.com/2014/05/blog-post_7204.html?m=1&fbclid=IwAR3U_MA8IzBWjU9ZVISVyJfEkkRFwpgs4126W2EmAKmBKZOO6I--R0BxmvU　兵庫県立考古博物館スタッフブログ]（[[兵庫県立考古博物館]]）。棺が納められた[[竪穴式石室]]の内壁と被葬者の[[頭蓋骨]]は赤く塗られ、4つに割られた[[内行花文鏡]]と槍鉋2点が[[副葬品|副葬]]され、墓壙内には[[土師器]]壺2個が据えられていた{{PDFlink|[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/material/files/group/43/tangovstajima.pdf 京丹後市制10周年記念、平成26年度丹後古代の里資料館秋季特別展示 但馬国府・国分寺館連携事業「丹後VS但馬 - 古代文物の徹底比較 - 」]}}（編集・発行 京丹後市立丹後古代の里資料館）。また、周辺には「但馬の王墓」とされる[[近畿地方]]最大級の[[円墳]]（[[茶すり山古墳]]）[https://www.city.asago.hyogo.jp/0000000417.html 近畿最大級の円墳 茶すり山古墳]（朝来市）があるなど、様々な点において大谷古墳との類似性が高い。 * その他の地域から女性人骨が出土した古墳 {| class="wikitable" style="font-size: small;" ! 地域 !! 年代 !! 古墳名 !! 墳形・墳長 !! 女性人骨のデータ |- | [[山形県]][[米沢市]] || 5世紀後半 || 戸塚山古墳137号墳 丹後は弥生時代後期に列島内外との交流を通じて独自の勢力圏を築き上げる。この時期は[[倭国大乱]]によって瀬戸内海の交易ルートが細くなっており、丹後を経由して大陸物資が畿内や東海にもたらされたと考えられる。丹後は耕作可能な土地が少なく農業生産力は限られているが、中国や朝鮮半島との鉄製品やガラスなどの交易や先進技術によって急速に発展していった。丹後系の土器は北近畿一帯に広がり、[[大風呂南墳墓]]・[[赤坂今井墳墓]]という王墓とも称される傑出した[[墳丘墓]]が出現し、後期末に繁栄は頂点を迎える。 弥生時代後期の伝統をひく方形墳は古墳時代前期に入っても引続き構築されている。大型の前方後円墳が出現する以前の古墳時代前期前半では、楕円形の大型円墳が王墓と考えられている。[[温江丸山古墳]]で三角縁神獣鏡や碧玉製腕飾りが出土しており、[[ヤマト政権]]との関係が示唆される。円墳に短い前方部がつく墳長100メートルの湧田山古墳は、[[ホケノ山古墳]]などと同形の[[纒向型前方後円墳]]とも目される。 丹後が繁栄した時代は2世紀後半から5世紀後半の約250年と考えられ、黒部銚子山古墳を最後に丹後では巨大な[[前方後円墳]]が作られなくなり、[[産土山古墳]]や[[離湖]]古墳といった規模が小さい[[円墳]]や[[方墳]]が作られるようになった{{Sfn|古代丹後の里資料館|2013|p=32}}5世紀末と第21代[[雄略天皇]]の代とが重なるこの時期が丹後のターニングポイントとなったと考えられる。[[雄略]]22年[[日本書紀]]によると浦嶋子が[[常世]]の国へ行った（最古の[[浦島伝説]]）と記される年に当たる。又、同年、[[伊勢神宮]]の社伝(止由気宮儀式帳）によると雄略天皇は[[神託]]により[[豊受大神]]を[[外宮]]へと[[遷宮]]をする。（京丹後市峰山町の[[比沼麻奈為神社]]が[[本地]]とされる[http://jinja.kojiyama.net/%E5%BC%8F%E5%86%85%E3%80%80%E6%AF%94%E6%B2%BC%E9%BA%BB%E5%A5%88%E7%82%BA%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE%EF%BC%88%E5%85%83%E4%BC%8A%E5%8B%A2%EF%BC%89/ 式内　比沼麻奈為神社（元伊勢）]（神社捨遺））雄略天皇は[[吉備氏]]を始め各地のの有力[[氏族]]を討つ、屈服させ、それを境に丹後に限らず地方の大型前方後円墳は築造されなくなった。古代史の『謎』を歩くp.20TJMOK宝島社 監修:[[関雄二]]丹後が最も栄えたであろう古墳時代前期に作られた大谷古墳は規模、築造時期などから網野銚子山古墳、神明山古墳と続く最高[[首長]]に連なる在地の小首長の墳墓と解される。 == 現地情報 == [[File:Ootani-kofun1.jpg|thumb|200px|大谷古墳公園]] '''所在地''' * 京都府京丹後市大宮町谷内小字大谷 墳丘を4分の1に復元した公園が整備されている{{PDFlink|[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/material/files/group/13/o_taniuchi2812.pdf ふるさとわがまちわが地域 大宮町谷内区]}} 京丹後市。古墳が存在した場所は、株式会社[[日進製作所|大宮日進]]の工場敷地内となっている[http://www.kiis.or.jp/kansaida/omiya/omiya03.html 大谷古墳] 関西デジタルアーカイブ。 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Reflist|2}} == 参考文献 == * {{Cite This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳}} |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |coordinates = 35.5733 |coordinates = 135.1014 |type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}}, {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}} |built = Early 5th century |burial = |area = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |burial = Female |burial goods = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |notes = Features distinctive burial goods associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|ja|京丹後市}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} classified as a {{ill|Keyhole-shaped tumulus|ja|前方後円墳|1=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpokoenfun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period Kofun groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|ja|築山古墳 (大分市)}} (Ōita Prefecture)== See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun}} * {{ill|Miko|lt=Female shamans in Japan|ja|巫女}} * {{ill|Tango Province|ja|丹後国}} == References == {{Reflist}} * Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)}}

During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=}} |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = [[:en:Kyōtango|Kyōtango]], {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Town|qq=}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |coordinates = 35.5733 |coordinates = 135.1014 |type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=}}, [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] |built = Early 5th century |burial = |area = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |burial = Female |burial goods = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |notes = Features distinctive burial goods associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Kyōtango|Kyōtango]], {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Town|qq=}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=}} classified as a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]], sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|Scallop Kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = [[File:Otanikofun.jpg|300px]] |caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = [[:en:Kyōtango|Kyōtango]], {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Town|qq=}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani |coordinates = 35.5733 |coordinates = 135.1014 |type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] |built = Early 5th century |burial = |area = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |burial = Female |burial goods = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |notes = Features distinctive burial goods associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Kyōtango|Kyōtango]], {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Town|qq=}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} classified as a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]], sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period Kofun groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukunoda Kofun|qq=}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * [[:en:Tsukiyama Kofun|Tsukiyama Kofun]] (Ōita Prefecture)== See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} * [[:en:Miko|Female shamans in Japan]] * [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]] == References == {{Reflist}} * Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|qq=}}

It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=Scallop Kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} classified as a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]], sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. This was added through [[Special:MassEditRegex]] to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|scallop-shaped kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = File:Otanikofun.jpg |caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyotango|qid=Q513897}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.57333333333333|N|135.1013888888889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] |built = Early 5th century |burial = |area = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |burial = Female |burial goods = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |notes = Features distinctive burial goods associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Kyōtango|Kyōtango]], {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Town|qq=|1=Ōmiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434439}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} classified as a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]], sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period Kofun groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukunoda Kofun|qq=}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * [[:en:Tsukiyama Kofun|Tsukiyama Kofun]] (Ōita Prefecture)== See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} * [[:en:Miko|Female shamans in Japan]] * [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]] == References == {{Reflist}} * Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|qq=}}

Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]], sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. This was added through to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|scallop-shaped kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = File:Otanikofun.jpg |caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyotango|WD=Q513897}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.57333333333333|N|135.1013888888889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] |built = Early 5th century |burial = |area = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |burial = Female |burial goods = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |notes = Features distinctive burial goods associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Kyōtango|Kyōtango]], {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Town|1=Ōmiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434439}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} classified as a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]], sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period Kofun groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukunoda Kofun|qq=}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * [[:en:Tsukiyama Kofun|Tsukiyama Kofun]] (Ōita Prefecture)== See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} * [[:en:Miko|Female shamans in Japan]] * [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]] == References == {{Reflist}} * Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|qq=}}

The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]], sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period Kofun groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukunoda Kofun|qq=}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * [[:en:Tsukiyama Kofun|Tsukiyama Kofun]] (Ōita Prefecture)== See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} * [[:en:Miko|Female shamans in Japan]] * [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]] == References == {{Reflist}} * Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|qq=}}

But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|scallop-shaped kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = File:Otanikofun.jpg |caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyotango|WD=Q513897}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.57333333333333|N|135.1013888888889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] |built = Early 5th century |burial = |area = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |burial = Female |burial goods = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |notes = Features distinctive burial goods associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Kyōtango|Kyōtango]], {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Town|1=Ōmiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434439}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} classified as a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]], sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period Kofun groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukunoda Kofun|qq=}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * [[:en:Tsukiyama Kofun|Tsukiyama Kofun]] (Ōita Prefecture)== See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} * [[:en:Miko|Female shamans in Japan]] * [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]] == References == {{Reflist}} * Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|qq=}}

This was added through to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|scallop-shaped kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = File:Otanikofun.jpg |caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyotango|WD=Q513897}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.57333333333333|N|135.1013888888889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]] |built = Early 5th century |burial = |area = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |burial = Female |burial goods = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |notes = Features distinctive burial goods associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in [[:en:Kyōtango|Kyōtango]], {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Town|1=Ōmiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434439}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} classified as a [[:en:Zenpokoenfun|Zenpokoenfun]]. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]], sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period Kofun groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukunoda Kofun|qq=}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * [[:en:Tsukiyama Kofun|Tsukiyama Kofun]] (Ōita Prefecture)== See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} * [[:en:Miko|Female shamans in Japan]] * [[:en:Tango Province|Tango Province]] == References == {{Reflist}} * Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|qq=}}

So a lot of these pages might not be marked on our wiki as having unknown parameters. But specifically keeping this comment here in case of import, these parameters should be added to [[Template:infobox ancient site]] rather than deleted from this draft or article[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:02, 28 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=I hope this is not too annoying but this article is gonna be placed under and there is a decent chance these unknown parameters are ones I want added to the main template like burial chamber structure and burial goods. Please do not use any bots that just remove the unknown parameters without looking at them. This was added through to all pages with the category so apologies if it was just some kind of an error like the image parameter being in Japanese[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 06:00, 27 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{Infobox ancient site|type = [[Zenpokoenfun]]|type = {{ill|scallop-shaped kofun|ja|帆立貝形古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} |name = Ōtani Kofun |image = File:Otanikofun.jpg |caption = Ōtani Kofun (reconstructed) |location = {{ill|Kyotango|WD=Q513897}} |coordinates = {{Coord|35.57333333333333|N|135.1013888888889|E|region:JP_type:landmark|display=inline,title}} |type = {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}} |built = Early 5th century |burial = |area = Total length: 32 meters Round rear: 26 meters diameter; 4 meters height Rectangular front: 19 meters width; 2.5 meters height |burial = Female |burial goods = |Cultural property = Tangible cultural property of Kyōtango |notes = Features distinctive burial goods associated with local female leadership }} '''Ōtani Kofun''' (大谷古墳) is an ancient tumulus located in {{ill|Kyōtango|en|Kyōtango|WD=Q513897|lt=Kyōtango}}, {{ill|Ōmiya Town|ja|大宮町 (京都府)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Town|1=Ōmiya|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11434439}}, Taniuchi, Ōtani. It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} classified as a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|en|Tango Province|WD=Q1054331|lt=Tango Province}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period Kofun groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukunoda Kofun|qq=}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|en|Tsukiyama Kofun|WD=Q11603501|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun}} (Ōita Prefecture)== See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} * {{ill|Miko|en|Miko|WD=Q1047139|lt=Female shamans in Japan}} * {{ill|Tango Province|en|Tango Province|WD=Q1054331|lt=Tango Province}} == References == {{Reflist}} * Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|qq=}}

It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} classified as a {{ill|Zenpokoenfun|en|Zenpokoenfun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpokoenfun|1=Zenpōkōenfun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|en|Tango Province|WD=Q1054331|lt=Tango Province|1=Tango Province}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section. No haniwa, fukiishi, or stepped construction were observed.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. * Total Length: 32 meters * Rear Mound: 26 meters in diameter, 4 meters in height * Front Mound: 19 meters in width, 2.5 meters in height == burial goods == burial goods include: * Bronze mirror: Diameter 10.8 cm * Magatama: High-quality green translucent jade * Glass beads: 33 blue glass beads * Iron sword: 43.7 cm in length * Iron axe: 7.2 cm in length * Yayoi pottery from earlier burial layers The sarcophagus was constructed from local granite and sealed with red pigment.Kyoto Shimbun, June 5, 2007. == Interred_individual == The preserved skeleton, though damaged, was identified as a middle-aged female based on pelvic structure. The cranial and facial features showed strong Jōmon traits, including a long skull and pronounced nasal structure.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=33}}. == Nearby Context == Female-centric leadership in the region is further evidenced by nearby sites such as {{ill|Ōmiya Shrine|ja|大宮売神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiya Shrine|qq=}}, where female deities are enshrined.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=33}}. Other notable sites include the Yayoi-period Kofun groups and smaller regional tumuli. == Related Sites == Comparable tumuli with female burials include: * {{ill|Mukunoda Kofun|ja|向野田古墳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mukunoda Kofun|qq=}} (Kumamoto Prefecture) * {{ill|Tsukiyama Kofun|en|Tsukiyama Kofun|WD=Q11603501|lt=Tsukiyama Kofun|1=Tsukiyama Kofun}} (Ōita Prefecture)== See Also == * {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} * {{ill|Miko|en|Miko|WD=Q1047139|lt=Female shamans in Japan|1=Miko}} * {{ill|Tango Province|en|Tango Province|WD=Q1054331|lt=Tango Province|1=Tango Province}} == References == {{Reflist}} * Scallop-shaped Kofun * {{ill|Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|ja|大谷古墳 (京丹後市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otani Kofun (Kyotango City)|qq=}}

It is a {{ill|Scallop-shaped tumulus|ja|帆立貝形古墳|1=scallop-shaped kofun|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Scallop-shaped tumulus|13=User:Immanuelle/scallop-shaped kofun|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} classified as a {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|en|Zenpō-kōen-fun|WD=Q11268718|lt=Zenpō-kōen-fun|1=Zenpō-kōen-fun}}. The excavated sarcophagus and burial goods are Historic Site1 as tangible cultural properties of Kyōtango.[https://www.city.kyotango.lg.jp/top/kanko_bunka_sports/bunkazai/3/3/4842.html C56 大谷古墳出土石棺及び出土遺物] (Kyōtango City Digital Museum). == Overview == The tumulus is located on the tip of a hill overlooking the Takeno River. Based on the excavated burial goods, it is estimated to have been constructed in the early 5th century. Notably, the tomb preserved a nearly complete skeleton of a middle-aged female, suggesting a possible era of female leadership in the mid-Kofun period.{{Sfn|Kyōtango Compilation Committee|2010|p=143}}. burial goods including symbols of power—mirrors, beads, and swords—were unearthed.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. The tomb's association with a female ruler led to comparisons with the legendary Himiko of {{ill|Tango Province|en|Tango Province|WD=Q1054331|lt=Tango Province|1=Tango Province}}, sparking public interest at the time of its discovery.{{Sfn|Tango Museum|2013|p=18}}. During relocation preparations, earlier Yayoi period Kofuns with overlapping structures were found beneath the tumulus.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987|p=7}}. == Excavation History == In 1987, during the development of an industrial park in Ōmiya Town, archaeological surveys confirmed the existence of the Ōtani Kofun.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. Although efforts were made to preserve surrounding sites, the central location of Ōtani Kofun necessitated full excavation and documentation.{{Sfn|Ōmiya Education Committee|1987}}. == burial == The tumulus is a scallop-shaped keyhole tumulus with a relatively short front section.
